rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: a cold self-study reader, or a fast operator scanning the deck, hits a header that could belong to any exercise and gets no orientation from it. Five of six `##` headers pass cleanly — 'Read the ticket for your bug' (L11), 'Read the conventions off the ticket' (L20), 'Write the close-out and send it' (L33), 'Double-check the voice' (L41) each name one concrete action; 'Anything can be reverse-engineered' (L45) is a claim-shaped header the body immediately supports (L47), and its bare, unqualified 'Anything' is covered by the L124 accept-note above (Antti 2026-08-30, explicitly re-affirmed: 'do not file the missing bullet as a defect') — not a truth-clause violation once that note is read. The sixth, '## What happened' (L50), is the rule's own listed failure shape near-verbatim — 'empty containers... head anything and name nothing.' Re-ran the corpus check this session: `grep -rl '^## What happened' curriculum/exercises/*.md` → this file only, out of 41 exercise files total (real command, this session; corpus has grown from 34 to 41 files since a prior run of this check, verdict unchanged). Harm is present but mild: this is the file's terminal beat, its two-sentence body (L52-54) is read immediately regardless of the header's specificity, and no mid-exercise navigation depends on the label. Filed non-blocking per template default ('other rules are TODO unless severe').

'Double-check the voice' (L43) is a self-check, not a forcing function. Neither of the two body edits since the last pin touches this row (both sit in the widget line and the closer bullet).
